content: coffee A controlled explosion on a film set close to the O₂ arena in London ignited a fire that consumed a van and caused damage to a car and a lorry. Fire crews were dispatched to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown just before 8 p.m. on Saturday. After about an hour, the blaze was brought under control by roughly twenty‑five firefighters, and no injuries were reported. Authorities said the fire stemmed from a pre‑arranged filming activity near the venue, which is scheduled to host performances by Niall Horan and Texas in the coming days. The London Fire Brigade posted on X that the fire in the Silvertown yard is now under control, noting that one vehicle was destroyed while most of a car and a lorry suffered damage, with no injury reports. They added that the incident originated from a controlled explosion on the set that spread beyond expectations, and firefighters acted swiftly to extinguish it, remaining on site for the rest of the evening. The yard is also situated near London’s cable‑car crossing over the River Thames. A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said they are aware of reports of explosions heard in the area around the O₂ in Greenwich.
